Independent analytical rendering oracle now reproduces cross-face mipmap contamination using only JavaFX public APIs, with a planar horizontal gray ramp and bijectively shuffled per-face atlas tiles. At 8192/32768/131072 triangles, exact-version ES2 control has maximum within-column gray spreads 16/41/41 and ramp RMSE 4.402/13.987/34.980. The one-line no-mipmap diagnostic reduces spreads to at most1 and RMSE0.296/0.370/0.406 (8-bit units). A nonempty-gradient assertion guards blank rendering. This specifically establishes the filtering contribution; real corrected unlit cortical images still contain grain, so it is not a full solution.

Retained source, six analytical PNGs, exact commands/class-origin logs and results: /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/output/brain-display/hidden-13/atlas-filtering/. Probe initially omitted an owning Scene and yielded blank frames; only corrected scene-attached runs establish the result. No native shared implementation edited and no OpenJFX fork adopted. Proper renderer work must preserve declared interpolation/association and acceptable update cost, not merely blur cortical data or average face values to hide artifacts.
